description: EIT* (Effort Informed Trees) searches each batch of random samples twice, like AIT*: a reverse search from the goal states computes a cost-to-go estimate `h` over the batch's *random geometric graph*, and a forward search from the start grows the tree. EIT*'s reverse search also estimates *effort*, the number of state checks still needed to reach the goal. It accepts an edge only if a few evenly spaced states on it pass a check, so its `h` already avoids the obstacles those sparse checks find. The forward search pops the edge with the least effort among those whose lower bound `g + c_hat + h` lies within a suboptimality factor of the smallest bound, so it finds a first solution with few collision checks. When the forward search finds that an edge of the reverse tree is invalid, the sparse checks per edge grow from `k` to `2k + 1` and the reverse search starts over. EIT* is anytime and almost-surely asymptotically optimal.

papers.authors: Marlin P. Strub, Jonathan D. Gammell
papers.title: Adaptively Informed Trees (AIT*) and Effort Informed Trees (EIT*): Asymmetric bidirectional sampling-based path planning
papers.venue: The International Journal of Robotics Research
